facts.business: Gujarat State Financial Corporation is a statutory body established under the State Financial Corporations Act, 1951, aimed at achieving balanced regional growth by extending financial assistance to first-generation entrepreneurs for micro and small-scale units in Gujarat, though it has discontinued main lending activities and is currently focused on recovery of dues.

auditor.name: J.H. Mehta & Co., Chartered Accountants
auditor.emphasis_or_qualification: Two qualifications: (a) Financial statements prepared on going concern basis despite completely eroded net worth and defaulted repayment obligations due to liquidity problems, not in accordance with AS-1; (b) Dues payable to Government of Gujarat subject to confirmation and adjustment, effect on interest and penal interest not ascertainable.

key_risks: Net worth completely eroded with defaulted repayment obligations due to liquidity problems
Going concern assumption questioned by auditors due to financial distress
Dues to Government of Gujarat subject to confirmation, with unascertainable interest and penal interest impact
Discontinued main lending activities, dependent solely on recovery of dues
Regulatory fines from BSE for absence of independent directors (corporate governance non-compliance)
100% net NPA ratio indicating entire loan portfolio is non-performing
Operating loss of -60.42% of average working funds
facts.related_party_note: Government of Gujarat and SIDBI are major shareholders; Government loans granted via budget provisions and Government Resolutions; Corporation moved Government to make loans interest-free from 1-7-2012; outstanding details submitted quarterly to administrative department; loan accounts verified by other authorities periodically.
